issue.title: [New Resource]: aws_marketplaceagreement_agreement
issue.body:
### What new functionality are you requesting?

* Service: Marketplace Agreement (`marketplaceagreement`)
* `aws_marketplaceagreement_agreement`

### Description

Subscribing an account to an AWS Marketplace offer is a console-only step today, so an account can't be built from Terraform alone when it uses Marketplace products. The case that hit me is EKS add-ons from Marketplace: `aws_eks_addon` for `datadog_operator` fails with `AddonSubscriptionNeeded` about 15 minutes into a new cluster's first apply, until someone accepts the offer in that account's Marketplace console.

The Marketplace Agreement API supports this for buyers now. `CreateAgreementRequest` (intent `NEW`) returns a quote, and `AcceptAgreementRequest` turns it into an agreement. `DescribeAgreement` and `GetAgreementTerms` read it back, and `CancelAgreement` cancels it. The SDK has it as [`service/marketplaceagreement`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/marketplaceagreement).

Plan, following the contributor guide:

1. PR adding the `marketplaceagreement` service client.
2. PR adding `aws_marketplaceagreement_agreement` and its list resource. Create is `CreateAgreementRequest` + `AcceptAgreementRequest`, Read is `DescribeAgreement` + `GetAgreementTerms`, Delete is `CancelAgreement`. Every argument change replaces the agreement. The identity is `agreement_id`.

What I found testing the API against a free offer (New Relic Kubernetes Operator):

* `CancelAgreement` returns `ValidationException` with reason `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION` for about 80 seconds after the agreement is accepted, then succeeds. Delete has to retry.
* An account can hold one active agreement per offer. A second `NEW` request for the same offer fails with `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION`, so the acceptance tests have to run serially.
* `DescribeAgreement` returns the offer ID but not the agreement proposal ID the agreement was created from, so an import can't fill in `agreement_proposal_id`.
* `CancelAgreement` on an agreement that's already cancelled succeeds.

AFAIK the acceptor can only cancel some agreements through the API (the buyer guide says usage agreements), so destroying a contract agreement will fail. That seems right to me: Terraform shouldn't be able to cancel a paid contract on its own.

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
# Datadog Operator EKS add-on (free)
resource "aws_marketplaceagreement_agreement" "datadog_operator" {
  agreement_proposal_id = "at-6nuclnsh88uc2s8hs1mjzr5eu"

  requested_term {
    id = "term-331241c92e99c39ff990052b4ae78d0165d892136e6af1aee8d55b9c28b540f9" # LegalTerm
  }

  requested_term {
    id = "term-17e763eebddabad9921f51d9360900fb6fd07cd91a0ab8699859b40d2cd7109a" # SupportTerm
  }
}

resource "aws_eks_addon" "datadog_operator" {
  cluster_name = aws_eks_cluster.example.name
  addon_name   = "datadog_operator"

  depends_on = [aws_marketplaceagreement_agreement.datadog_operator]
}
```

### References

* [Work with the Agreement API as a buyer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/work-with-agreement-api-buyer.html)
* [CreateAgreementRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_CreateAgreementRequest.html)
* [`github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/marketplaceagreement`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/marketplaceagreement)

### Would you like to implement the enhancement?

Yes
